# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 77 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_077_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 77

**1** Jesus said: "I am the light that is over all things. I am the All.

**2** From me the All came forth, and to me the All attained.

**3** Split a piece of wood; I am there. Lift up the stone, and you will find me there."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** This is arguably the most theologically rich saying in Thomas and one of the most discussed texts in early Christian studies.

**"The All"** — *pterf*: capitalized in SOPHIA to mark it as a cosmic term. The All comes from Jesus and returns to Jesus — a circular cosmological statement.

**"To me the All attained"** — *attain/aphikneomai*: the All "attaining" or "arriving at" its source — the eschatological return. LOGOS's "have returned" is interpretively richer but goes slightly beyond the Coptic.

**"Split a piece of wood / Lift up the stone"** — these lines assert divine immanence in the material world — the sacred hidden in the ordinary. They appear in a different location in P.Oxy 1 (Greek fragment), confirming their early circulation.

**Synoptic Parallels:** The "I am" structure echoes John's Gospel but with a distinctly cosmic, panentheistic character. No Synoptic parallel exists. This is the definitive Thomas self-revelation of Jesus.
